 Three NC Chili's customers treated for chemical burns after margarita mix-up
 A Chili's in Forest City was temporarily closed after customers suffered chemical burns from margaritas mistakenly made with a degreasing agent.

 By Justin Burnette, WRAL News
 The Foothills Health District temporarily suspended the food service permit of a Chili's Grill & Bar in Forest City, N.C., after multiple customers suffered chemical burns after drinking margaritas mistakenly prepared with a cleaning agent, according to the Foothills Health District. 
 The Foothills Health District said it happened after someone mistakenly brought an unlabeled container to the restaurant's bar area. The health district said a contracted worker was using the container to help power-wash the building.
 Other WRAL Top Stories
 On Wednesday, an employee used the unlabeled container that they thought was sugar to prep the margarita station. The substance was later identified as a "granulated degreasing chemical."
 According to health officials, three customers who ordered margaritas immediately experienced chemical burns around their mouths after consuming the drinks. Two employees also tasted the drinks and reported similar symptoms. 
 Following the incident, the Foothills Health District suspended the restaurant's food service permit and directed staff to clean and sanitize affected equipment, surfaces and preparation areas. 
 Environmental health specialists completed their investigation on Oct. 29 and reinstated the restaurant’s food service permit after corrective measures were taken, officials said.
